title: Randomized SVD Approximations for Spectral Co-Clustering of Word-Document Matrices
summary: The methods replace the full SVD used in normalized spectral co-clustering of word-document matrices with a random-projection randomized SVD or a partial SVD combined with element-wise sampling. The cost is approximation error in the spectral embedding, which can degrade cluster quality, and the added implementation complexity of maintaining two algorithm variants. The sampling-based variant can fail on already sparse text matrices, where it provides limited benefit, so the choice of approximation depends on the sparsity structure of the data.
rationale: This is classical unsupervised text mining rather than LLM work, but if the reader runs spectral co-clustering at scale, the random-projection variant is cheap to implement on a single machine and warrants workload-specific validation of cluster quality against the runtime saved.

claims.statement: The methods replace the full SVD used in normalized spectral co-clustering of word-document matrices with a random-projection randomized SVD or a partial SVD combined with element-wise sampling. The cost is approximation error in the spectral embedding, which can degrade cluster quality, and the added implementation complexity of maintaining two algorithm variants. The sampling-based variant can fail on already sparse text matrices, where it provides limited benefit, so the choice of approximation depends on the sparsity structure of the data.
Both randomized approximations reduce runtime relative to the full-SVD baseline, with the random-projection variant the more reliable across tested settings; no specific speedup factor is stated.
